objective: Adversarially review the Stage 3 experimental Slide IR draft for the QueueZero benchmark. Try to break the architecture before implementation. Identify missing semantics, renderer leakage, unstable identity, change-impact failures, editability traps, evidence/provenance gaps, and cases where the same IR cannot fairly drive image-first, native-vector, and hybrid variants. Do not redesign the entire product unless a flaw requires it; propose the smallest schema changes that make the controlled experiment trustworthy.
questions: Does the IR cleanly separate reasoning semantics, semantic visual structure, render planning, and realization, or are renderer concerns leaking into upstream semantics?
Are semantic object IDs, evidence IDs, relationship IDs, asset IDs, and realization mappings sufficient for stable incremental edits and fact-to-PPTX-object change-impact tracing?
What semantic information would be irrecoverably lost after export or local manual editing with the current schema?
Is the evidence model sufficient for raw facts, derived values/simple arithmetic, assumptions, inferences, uncertainty, source spans, and conflicting/revised evidence?
Can the relationship model prevent misleading visual implications such as correlation being drawn as causation, or evidence being connected to outcomes it does not prove? What is missing?
Are grouping, ownership, nested objects, repeated components, ordering/z-order, and constraints represented strongly enough without prematurely encoding layout coordinates?
What data model is missing for charts and tables if Stage 3 later needs true editable chart/table objects?
What information is needed to support deterministic text fitting, overflow handling, and localized title/metric edits without layout cascades?
How should generated hero visuals declare semantic exclusions, text-free zones, safe crop areas, or composition anchors so bounded regeneration does not interfere with native overlays?
Does allowed_render_lanes/preferred_render_lane belong in the semantic object itself or in a separate capability/routing policy? Give a concrete recommendation.
How should renderer-specific capability constraints and fallbacks be represented while keeping the semantic IR renderer-agnostic?

Can the current change-impact contract actually guarantee that 76%→81%, screenshot replacement, accent recolor, KPI move, title resize, deletion, sponsor-logo insertion, diagram wording edits, and hero-only regeneration remain local? Identify counterexamples.
Can the same IR fairly drive the image-first baseline without giving native/hybrid variants extra semantic information unavailable to the image renderer, or is the benchmark biased?
Which fields are unnecessary complexity for Stage 3 and should be deferred?
What minimum changes must be made before freezing the experimental IR and beginning the 3x3 benchmark?
expected_output: Critical architecture flaws ranked by severity
Text fitting and bounded image regeneration requirements
Minimum schema patch list before Stage 3 build
